title: Homology represented by the shifted free module with its cocycle formula
statement: Let k be any commutative ring in universe u and choose the derived category of ModuleCat k in universe u [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. Let S(n) be the single complex with free rank-one module k in integer degree n, equivalently k[-n]. There is a family of k-linear equivalences Hom_D(Q(S(n)),A) to H^n(A), for all derived objects A and all integers n, natural for postcomposition in A. If f:S(n) to K is a chain map and z is a degree-n cycle of K whose inclusion equals the value at 1 of f in degree n (transported through singleObjXSelf), the equivalence sends Q(f) to homologyFunctorFactors.inv applied to homology projection of z. This is exactly Nonempty CupHomologyRepresentability k.

source.place: Lemma 13.19.8: Hom from a bounded-above projective complex in the homotopy and derived categories; Tag 068G: cohomology classes represented by cocycles

proof.text: The single free module S(n) is bounded above and projective in every degree. Apply the bounded-projective localization bijection to identify Hom_D(Q(S(n)),Q(K)) with chain maps S(n) to K modulo homotopy, without any boundedness on K.

A chain map from S(n) is uniquely determined by the image of 1 in degree n, which lies in ker(d^n); a chain homotopy changes that image by a boundary, and every boundary arises in this way. Evaluation therefore identifies chain maps modulo homotopy with homology, k-linearly and bijectively. Transport by homologyFunctorFactors. All derived objects have complex representatives; the evaluation identification commutes with quasi-isomorphisms and postcomposition, so it descends to a natural family on A. Evaluating Q(f) with the specified generator gives exactly homology projection of z transported by the inverse factorization iso. This includes every integer degree and the zero ring.
